Coastal Plain Sands, MASW, Soil Stability, Velocity Variations.

As part of the efforts to examine the elastic and engineering properties of the subsurface sequence at a proposed new power plant site in Edo State, a geophysical survey involving Multichannel Analysis of Surface Waves (MASW) was carried out. The MASW was adopted to determine the vertical and lateral variations in velocity beneath each seismic line. The MASW was carried out on two seismic lines each trending NE-SW. A geophone interval of 3 m was used, and the length of the seismic lines ranged from 60 â€“ 90 m. The ES-3000 seismograph was used for the surface wave data acquisition and the Shear-Wave velocity structures of the area were obtained through the inversion of the acquired surface wave data. The one dimensional (1D) S-Wave velocity profiles along the lines were diagnostic of generally low velocity lithologies that suggest sand, clayey sand and sandy clay formations with relatively varying thicknesses. The subsurface layers delineated had shear-wave velocity values in the range of 63-400 m/s. They were classified using the NEHRP Seismic Site Classification, and all of them were in the range of stiff soil to soft clay soil. The bulk moduli (k) for these soils were in the range of 3.22-3.98 GPa. This depicts relatively low strength of the subsurface materials. The shear moduli (Î¼) values range from 7.15-7.43 MPa, which is indicative of low to moderate strength. The information provided in this study will aid the structural engineer or architect in foundation design of the proposed power plant. From the results of this study, it is concluded that although the subsurface layers are of relatively low strength, with the right intervention of the civil engineer, a suitable foundation can be designed for the gas plant.

When relating earthquakes or seismic energy to global warming, shouldn't any increase actually have started at the beginning of the Industrial Revolution in the 1800's -- or at the end of the last ice age about 10,000 years ago? Any paper, like the one you're debunking, trying to link the two things -- hot air and seismicity -- should go back a little farther than the last several decades! Your graph actually shows an overall flat line or even downward trend overall since 1900.

I think most of the people looking for a secular increase are hoping to see a signal that God is warming up for an end-of-days finale.

Back in the ancient days when I was a grad student in seismology: Richter scale was the log of the amplitude on a standard seismograph at a standard distance. The short period seismograph was used, and the amplitude only looked at the first couple of seconds of the wave train. A magnitude eight typically takes a couple of minutes to rupture along hundreds of KM of fault, so the Richter scale was really a measurement of the energy at initiation point of the quake.

Martin says: "A random question - isn't the real trend (over millions of years) in fact going to be downwards as the Earth ages? I'm guessing over a century or so that's not going to be noticeable, mind."

That's an interesting thought ... I guess I would put that trend in the billions of years instead of millions ... the plate tectonic 'machine' will keep churning for a long time to come. At least, that's my speculation.

Determining the S-wave velocity using refraction microtremors technique

The present study uses the Refraction Microtremors (ReMi) method to determine and calculate the S-wave seismic velocity with depth for Ben Ezra Synagogue. This is important to determine the depth to the bedrock [any solid rock underlying the soil with S-wave > 765 m/s, the national databases of the US Geological Survey (USGS)]. Louie [20] explained that, the refraction microtremor technique is based on two fundamental ideas: (1) common seismic-refraction recording equipment, set out in a way almost identical to shallow P-wave refraction surveys, can effectively record surface waves at frequencies as low as 2 Hz; and (2) a simple, two-dimensional slowness–frequency (p–f) transform of a microtremor record can separate Rayleigh waves from other seismic arrivals and allow recognition of true phase velocity against apparent velocities [20,21,22,23,24].

Data acquisition and interpretation

ES-3000 seismograph was used for the measurement of background ‘noise’ at Ben Ezra Synagogue and its surrounding area. Three profiles were conducted around Ben Ezra Synagogue, as shown in Fig. (6). ReMi analysis presented herein was developed using 12 channels (14 Hz, geophones) set along a straight-line array with different receiver spacing. Receiver spacing for ReMi profiles used. Unfiltered, 30 files of 20 s each were record for surrounding “noise” [25,26,27,28].

The method was applied using the well Known Optim Software for ReMi data modeling. Figures 7 and 8 show the dispersion curve and spectrum P-F image (Remi Spectral ratio of surface waves) for ReMi profiles ReMi-1 to ReMi-3 respectively. The excluded models for S-wave velocity with depth for ReMi profiles ReMi-1 to Remi-3 are shown in Figs. 9, 10, 11. Table 1. Summarizes the receiver spacing for ReMi profiles used. It is noticed that outside Ben Ezra Synagogue, the S-wave velocity detected is about 900 m/s for average depth of about 6.5 m, and reach to 160

DSSTech's home automation system functionalities

Alarm system control

The system allows to protect home from theft attempts through volumetric, magnetic and/or inertial detectors and using commercial internal and external alarms.
It is possible to activate/switch off the alarm system using an electronic key, a numeric keyboard, touch-screen display or through an SMS sent to the GSM device.
The GSM device can inform about the status/events of the alarm system sending back SMS on the mobile phone (for example launch of the alarm signals, entry door open, etc…)

Consumption / Energy saving

Currently the system can supervise the energy spent by each plant, monophase or triphase, which is measured before the electricity meter of the provider. We can display on the touch screen the energy consumption evolution through the day, the week, month or year, also history of previous years, time bands and related rates of the energy provider, power factor and instant operative power of the past 24 hours on a diagram.
If correctly set up with the rates of the energy provider, we can estimate quite precisely the energy consumption of small devices.

Photovoltaic system

On the touch-screen it is controlled and displayed the energy produced by the photovoltaic system. It is measured in an independent and accurate way at the output of the inverter with all the control functions of the system: energy, energy fed in system, self-consumed energy, GSE incentives, percentage of plant productivity, cost and amortisartion time of the installed system and malfunction alarms.
The alarms are also remotely managed on smartphone so you have at all times proper monitoring of the entire plant. The display also shows the curve of productivity's optimization through solarimeter and PV panels temperature sensors.

Audio system

Our audio wired wireless system allows to provide up to 4 different STEREO sources, otherwise 8 MONO sources on each location. Each area controlled by a final device can be reached by the sound of any of the sources and it is possible to settle its volume, its tones or change source.
It is possible to manage all the above options using a infrared remote control on each area.

GSM control

This system allows, using a mobile phone, to control all the automation system sending/receiving advisory SMS (status, alarm warnings,  etc…) or control SMS
